kb.mainBookDesc: The card's main book — always on. Put the world, the protagonist and the rules every route needs here. (This equals your single lorebook today.)
kb.allDesc: Entries from every knowledge base, merged in their actual send order — drag here to reorder entries across books.
kb.bindingsPanelDesc: The dedicated knowledge base for all frontend-controlled entries — add a <LoreButton> / <LoreSwitch> in your frontend code (Custom UI) and an entry is created here. The entry enters the prompt only while the player turns its control on.
kb.listHint: A card can hold several independent knowledge bases. Each can be enabled/disabled as a whole and optionally bound to a variable / frontend / opening. Entries live inside each book.
kb.noVars: No variables yet — add some in Variables first to gate this book by condition.
kb.alwaysHint: This book is always on (as long as it's enabled).
kb.manualHint: No variable rule: you control this book's on/off — put a button in your frontend, or flip the enable switch above. Binding is optional.
kb.modeGreetingHint: This book is active only when one of the selected openings is the session's starting message. Perfect for per-route independent knowledge.
kb.greetingNone: No openings yet — add some in First Message first

worldbooks.title: Worldbooks
worldbooks.description: Group entries into activatable lore modules — a Core book that's always on, plus per-route / per-scene books that switch on by variable conditions. Only active books reach the AI, so a big multi-world card stays within budget.
worldbooks.coreNote: Entries with no worldbook belong to the always-on "Core" book. Add a worldbook below and assign entries to it so they activate only on a condition.
worldbooks.emptyDesc: Create a worldbook to gate a whole set of entries (its own presets, examples, lore) behind a variable — perfect for routes, chapters and scenes.
worldbooks.alwaysHint: This worldbook is always active — its entries are always eligible (same as the Core book).
worldbooks.noVars: No variables defined yet — add variables first to gate this worldbook.
worldbooks.assignHint: Pick which worldbook each entry belongs to. "Core" = always on. Greetings are managed in First Message.

firstMessage.title: First Message
firstMessage.description: The opening message shown when a player starts a new session. Add multiple greetings for players to swipe through.
firstMessage.placeholder: Write the opening message your players will see...
firstMessage.noFirstMessageDesc: The first message sets the scene — it introduces the setting, characters, and gives players something to respond to.
firstMessage.initialVarsHint: Variables to seed when a player starts on this opening. Use this to make an opening a route/scenario preset — e.g. set route = "mayu" so the matching worldbook (and frontend view) activate from turn one.
firstMessage.initialVarsReadonlyHint: Seeded when a player picks this opening. Edit these under Variables → Per-opening values.
firstMessage.noInitialVars: No variables seeded for this opening — it uses defaults.

entries.title: Lorebook
entries.description: All content injected into the prompt — characters, system instructions, scenarios, lore
entries.noEntriesDesc: The lorebook holds everything the AI needs — character descriptions, world lore, system instructions, and more.

tokenBreakdown.greetingHint: Sent once at session start, before the player's first message.
tokenBreakdown.greetingHintMulti: {{count}} greetings — the player sees one per session, not all of them. This row sums every greeting in the lorebook.
tokenBreakdown.alwaysSentHint: Entries marked "Always Send". Included in the prompt every turn — this is your predictable per-turn cost floor.
tokenBreakdown.keywordTriggeredHint: Fires only when the keywords match recent messages, capped by the lorebook token budget. Variable cost from 0 up to this number per turn.
tokenBreakdown.dormantHint: Enabled but never fires: not set to Always Send AND has no keywords. The matcher silently skips these. Usually a setup mistake — add keywords or enable Always Send.
tokenBreakdown.toggleHint: Click to expand or collapse the per-bucket breakdown
tokenBreakdown.healthCaution: Getting big. Worth checking: is the same setting written across several entries? Are you repeating 'don't do X' (which can make the AI fixate on X)? Are you writing things the engine already handles? Pick one spot and trim it.
tokenBreakdown.healthHeavy: The less you write, the better the AI listens — when there's too much, it loses the point. Try merging duplicated settings, compressing long example lists into a single principle + word list, and dropping rules the engine already enforces.

entries.scanDepthHint: Number of recent messages to scan (1 - 50)
entries.recursionDepthHint: Max depth for cascading entry triggers. 0 = disabled.
entries.name: Name
entries.depthHint: Injected this many messages before the latest message
entries.positionHint: Sort order within this section. Lower = higher up. Drag to reorder automatically.
entries.keywordsHint: This entry activates when these keywords appear in recent messages. Press Enter to insert a separator; comma (,), fullwidth (，) and 顿号 (、) all work.
entries.whenConditionsHint: Fire this entry when game variables match — even with no keywords. Combine with keywords for AND logic.
entries.variableBindExplain: This entry is active only while the conditions below are met (prompt injection / Custom UI slots). Enabled and Always Send do not apply.
entries.variableBindNoVars: Define variables in the Variables section first
entries.worldbookHint: Which lore module this entry belongs to. Entries in a worldbook only reach the AI while that worldbook is active. Manage worldbooks in the Worldbooks section.

triggerBoard.title: When the AI sees each entry
triggerBoard.description: Each card shows the conditions that make it enter the AI prompt. Combined triggers must all be true.
triggerBoard.alwaysSendHint: Injected every turn — stable cache prefix
triggerBoard.keywordsHint: Fire when keywords appear in recent chat
triggerBoard.frontendHint: Active while a custom UI trigger point is mounted
triggerBoard.combinedEmpty: No entries require multiple trigger types yet
triggerBoard.frontendEmpty: Add UI trigger points in custom UI code — bindings will auto-create entries here
triggerBoard.activationMount: Conditional render: {open && <LoreSlot id="x" />} — visible means active
triggerBoard.activationClick: Button toggles state that controls whether the trigger point exists
triggerBoard.activationVariable: useEffect when a variable changes — show the trigger point when true
triggerBoard.activationTab: Tabs / panels — render the trigger point only on the active view
triggerBoard.activationScroll: Scroll into view — IntersectionObserver then mount
triggerBoard.activationHover: Hover / long-press reveals a region that mounts the trigger point

entries.keywordsEnterHint: Press Enter to add the next keyword (commas , ，、 also work)
entries.alwaysSendWarningDesc: Entries in this section form a stable prompt prefix that LLM providers cache across turns. Making it keyword-triggered means the prefix changes when keywords match, reducing cache efficiency and increasing costs.
entries.cacheWarningDesc: Keyword-triggered entries outside the Chat History section break prompt caching. When the keyword fires, the entire cached prefix is invalidated, forcing every turn to re-process all prior context. Move this entry to Chat History (with a depth) to keep the cache intact.

tagManager.title: Tag Manager

sendAsOptions.assistantHint: AI thinks it said this. For prefill & CoT bypass.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Define game state variables to track player stats, items, and story progress.
variables.noVariablesDesc: The AI reads and updates variables during gameplay using bracket syntax like [health: -10].
variables.behaviorRulesHint: Describe in plain language when and how this variable should change — the engine handles telling the AI which update directive to emit. You don't need to write commands like "set hp=..." here.

aiAccessHint.write: Shown to the AI every turn and updatable via its directives — for state only the AI can judge (affinity, mood).
aiAccessHint.read: Shown to the AI with a read-only marker so it narrates the value, but AI directives targeting it are dropped — drive it from behaviors or your custom UI.
aiAccessHint.none: Never sent to the AI. Still drives conditions, behaviors and your custom UI — for ledgers, counters and other bookkeeping.

variables.manualHint: Toggle it at runtime from a behavior via {{path}} (true/false). While off, the variable leaves the AI prompt and player UI but keeps its value.
variables.conditionsHint: Active only while these conditions match — the value is kept while inactive.
variables.greetingHint: Active only in sessions started from the checked openings.
variables.jsonPreserved: Valid JSON · Key order and formatting preserved
variables.jsonInvalidDraft: Invalid JSON. Check brackets, quotes and commas.
variables.jsonSaveBlocked: Fix the JSON default value for “{{name}}” before saving.
variables.jsonHint: Must be valid JSON (object or array). Use double quotes around field names and string values.
variables.idTaken: That ID is already used by another variable — renamed to {{id}}

openingValues.title: Per-opening initial values
openingValues.hint: Each opening can override a variable's starting value. Cells left on “default” use the variable's default. This is the one place to set per-opening values — the First Message panel mirrors it read-only.
openingValues.setOverride: Set a value for this opening
openingValues.emptyDesc: Add at least one variable and one opening (in First Message) to set per-opening starting values.

welcome.title: Welcome to the Advanced Editor!
welcome.body:
I'm Mushie! This is the workshop where world cards are made.
Follow me for a lap — you'll try every important spot hands-on!

nav.title: This is the navigation
nav.body: The editor has three areas: Content for your story and rules, Presentation for visuals and sound, and Publish for your card's public face. Let's go top to bottom!

goFirstMessage.title: Start with the First Message
goFirstMessage.body: The first message is what players see the moment they enter your world. Click here to open it!

createGreeting.title: Create your first message
createGreeting.body: Click this button to create your very first opening message!

greetingContent.title: Write it here
greetingContent.body: Write your opening here — the user and char macros (wrapped in double curly braces) stand for the player and the character. Multiple first messages become selectable opening routes!

goLorebook.title: Next: the Lorebook
goLorebook.body: The lorebook holds your world's knowledge. Click here to take a look!

kbBooks.title: Your books
kbBooks.body: This slim strip on the left holds this card's books. The Main book is always active — just put your lore in it. Once you're comfortable you can add more books toggled by condition. For now, let's write into the Main book!

entriesAdd.title: Add an entry
entriesAdd.body: Worldbuilding, character sheets, rules — you write them all as individual entries. Click "Add" to create your first one!

entryContent.title: Title for you, content for the AI
entryContent.body: The name is just a label to keep yourself organized — the AI never sees it. What matters is the content: write the actual lore there. Add keywords, and the entry is only sent to the AI when the conversation touches that topic — precise and efficient.

goVariables.title: Now, Variables
goVariables.body: Variables track numbers that change during play. Click to check them out!

varsAdd.title: Add a variable
varsAdd.body: Affection, gold, quest progress — store them all as variables. The AI and your custom UI can read and write them. Click "Add variable" to create one!

varsFields.title: Setting up a variable
varsFields.body: Give it a display name, pick a type (number/text/toggle), and set the default value each playthrough starts with. The best part is "Behavior rules": tell the AI in plain words when and how the value should change — like "gain 5 affection on an intimate moment" — and it follows along.

goBehaviors.title: Next: Behaviors
goBehaviors.body: Behaviors are your world's automation rules. Click here to enter!

behaviorsAdd.title: Add a behavior
behaviorsAdd.body: Click "Add behavior" and create a rule!

behaviorsDetail.title: How a behavior works
behaviorsDetail.body: Every behavior = When… (event) + If… (conditions) + Then… (actions). For example: when a variable changes, if affection reaches 100, then switch the BGM and unlock a new entry. Configure the three parts right here.

presentationSkip.title: Presentation: advanced stuff
presentationSkip.body: Custom UI, Audio and Assets under Presentation are advanced — building your card its own interface and soundtrack. Come back when you're comfortable; the Creator Guide has full tutorials. Skipping for now!

overviewTitle.title: Name your card
overviewTitle.body: The Overview is your card's public face. The title is the first thing players see in the hub — make it a good one!

overviewDescription.title: Write a description
overviewDescription.body: The description shows on your card's detail page and supports Markdown. Explain the gameplay and highlights so players want to click in!

publish.title: Publish your world
publish.body: When you're ready, click here at the top right to submit for publishing. Once approved it appears in the hub for everyone to play!

save.title: Remember to save
save.body: Save any time here (Ctrl+S works too). A little dot on the button reminds you when there are unsaved changes.

studio.title: One more thing: the Studio
studio.body: Click here to enter the Studio, where an AI assistant is on standby — tell it your ideas and it writes entries, builds variables, wires behaviors, even creates a whole custom UI for you. Whenever you're stuck, let it take over!

menuAdvanced.title: More advanced sections
menuAdvanced.body: The menu also holds Custom UI, Audio and Assets — advanced tools for giving your card its own interface and soundtrack. Come back when you're comfortable; the Creator Guide has full tutorials!

saveM.title: Remember to save
saveM.body: Tap here at the top right to save any time. A little dot on the button reminds you when there are unsaved changes.

finish.title: Off you go!
finish.body: That's the whole lap! Hit PLAY any time to playtest your world. For a deeper dive, open the Creator Guide at the top right — and find me in the ⋮ menu to replay this tour. Have fun building!

kbBooksM.title: Your books
kbBooksM.body: This row at the top holds this card's books. The Main book is always active — just put your lore in it. Once you're comfortable you can add more books toggled by condition. For now, let's write into the Main book!

publishM.title: Publish your world
publishM.body: When you are ready, tap here to submit for publishing. Once approved it appears in the hub for everyone to play!

menuOpen.title: The section menu
menuOpen.body: Every area of the editor — First Message, Lorebook, Variables, Behaviors and more — lives in this menu. Tap it open!

menuPick.title: Enter First Message
menuPick.body: See? These are all the areas. Let us start with First Message — tap it to enter!
